messages:
maria: Quick proposal on KV cache granularity + eviction. TL;DR: switch to fixed allocation buckets (16KB) + size-aware LRU + per-request token caps. Aim: reduce fragmentation, lower OOM incidence during aggressive prefill, and keep decode latencies stable.

sam: short version pls + numbers? :thinking:

maria: numbers from the perf run on dev-gpu-03 (batching load @ 400 qps, seq len 1024):
- baseline (variable entries): fragmentation ~37%, peak GPU RSS 31.2 GiB, OOMs: 4/6 runs
- proposal (16KB buckets): fragmentation ~12%, peak GPU RSS 26.7 GiB, OOMs: 0/6 runs
- p95 token latency: baseline 28ms -> proposal 30ms (small regress), p50 unchanged

raj: those are promising. where did the 16KB come from? tried other sizes?

maria: we swept bucket sizes: 4KB, 8KB, 16KB, 64KB. tradeoffs:
- 4KB: best for small-entry density but higher allocator overhead and slightly worse throughput
- 8KB: decent, fragmentation ~18%
- 16KB: sweet spot on our workloads (many ~8-20KB KV blobs)
- 64KB: low fragmentation but waste on small entries -> higher peak RSS for short responses

lina: experimental config used (dev cluster):
```json
{
  "kv_cache": {
    "allocation_bucket_bytes": 16384,
    "eviction_policy": "size_aware_lru",
    "per_request_token_cap": 512,
    "prefill_strategy": "adaptive", 
    "prefill_threshold_tokens": 64
  }
}
```

perfbot: perfbot: profiling summary attached. key outputs:
- kernel selection: no change (cuBLAS/transform fused kernels unchanged)
- decode throughput: -3% steady-state for single-request streamer under bucketed alloc, but batching throughput unchanged
- allocator metrics: free_fragmented_bytes reduced by 62%

sam: how does this affect prefill vs decode decisions? prefill used to reduce decode stalls but triggers many small KV inserts which fragment.

maria: correct. With bucketing we can prefill more aggressively because inserts coalesce into bucket slots instead of many tiny allocations. but prefill still increases pressure: we added a per-request cap to avoid pathological bursts (we hit a few production cases where single user hit 20k token prefill).

raj: eviction policy details? what is size_aware_lru here?

maria: size_aware_lru = LRU that prefers evicting entries with the highest bytes/token ratio when under memory pressure. heuristic: score = recency_weight * age_rank + size_weight * (bytes / tokens). tuned weights: recency_weight=0.6, size_weight=0.4. intent: keep small dense entries, evict big bloated KV entries first.

lina: did you consider segmented LRU or frequency-based (LFU) variants?

maria: we prototyped seg-LRU but it kept cold small entries around due to frequency buckets and increased metadata overhead. LFU caused retained stale heavy entries in long-lived workloads. size_aware_lru hit the best tradeoff in our traces.

perfbot: microtrace snippet from an induced OOM on baseline:
```
[2026-02-17 13:12:11] alloc 0x7f.. size=29240 -> slab split -> fragmentation++
[2026-02-17 13:12:11] prefill insert 42KB key -> fails -> fallback to decode path -> latency spike
[2026-02-17 13:12:11] OOM triggered in workspace allocator
```
With buckets the same trace becomes:
```
[2026-02-17 13:12:11] alloc bucket 16KB idx=3 -> reused
[2026-02-17 13:12:11] prefill insert coalesced -> no slab split
```

sam: rollout plan? metrics to watch?

maria: canary 5% on Dedicated clusters for 24h with automatic rollback if: OOM_count increases, p95 token latency > +20%, or user error rate increases >0.5%. Observe fragmentation_ratio, peak_RSS, avg_batch_tokens, and eviction_rate.

raj: any perf regression tests failing? we saw a small p95 bump. is that acceptable?

lina: p95 +3-5% for single-stream is acceptable given 15% reduction in token-cost and near-elimination of OOMs. ops confirmed customer-facing alerts were driven by OOMs not p95.

maria: action items:
- sam: add canary config + gating in rollout infra (due EOD)
- raj: add unit tests for bucket allocator invariants + fragmentation metric (2d)
- lina: run a longer 72h soak on prefill-heavy trace set and upload perf logs
- perfbot: schedule nightly regression with bucket sizes 8/16/64KB for next 3 nights

sam: will do. tagging @infra-bot to create canary. :+1:

infra-bot: infra-bot: created canary rollout ticket INF-4521, targeting Dedicated-canary-5pct. link: https://redwood.internal/INF-4521

maria: thanks all. if canary looks good we can consider defaulting bucketed alloc for Dedicated and leaving hosted API on adaptive mode for a bit longer.

raj: one more thought — add a fast-path free list for tiny entries (<4KB) to avoid touching buckets for very small ephemeral KVs. low complexity and might recover perf for chat workloads.

maria: good idea. add as follow-up spike.

lina: sounds good. I'll start the soak today. :rocket:
